record.title: Vertex-transitive balanced graph cycle conjecture
record.statement: Let $X$ be a connected vertex-transitive balanced graph. An **$(l,t)$-cycle** is the graph described by the paper's preceding definitions. **Vertex-transitive balanced graph cycle conjecture.** $X$ is an $(l,t)$-cycle. The conjecture is supported by computer searches, including an exhaustive analysis of the graphs on Gordon Royle's web page. If true, it would imply that the only connected vertex-transitive balanced graphs of odd degree are the complete bipartite graphs.
record.source_name: Joy Morris, Pablo Spiga and Kerri Webb, “Balanced Cayley graphs and balanced planar graphs”, arXiv:0707.0155 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.0155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2007).

record.title: The conjectural constant in the metric-graph bound
record.statement:
Let $g\geq2$, let $\overline{\Gamma}$ be a pm-graph of genus $g$, and retain the notation of the proposition in the source: $A$ is the constant in the proposition's upper bound for the relevant graph polynomial ratio.

**Conjecture on the optimal constant.** One may take

$$
A=\frac{7(g-1)^2}{6g(3g-5)}.
$$

Equivalently, the metric-graph conjecture above holds with

$$
c(g)=\frac{g-1}{27g}.
$$

This would give a strong uniform conjectural lower bound for $\varphi(\overline{\Gamma})$ and, through the paper's reductions, an effective geometric Bogomolov bound. The claim is presented as a conjectural strengthening of the verified low-genus estimates.
record.source_name: X. W. C. Faber, “The Geometric Bogomolov Conjecture for Small Genus Curves”, arXiv:0803.0855 (2009).

record.title: Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and projective dimension for ideals of poset homomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be posets with $s$ and $t$ connected components, respectively. Write $\mathfrak{a}(P)$ and $\mathfrak{a}(Q)$ for the invariants appearing in the proposed formulas, and let $\mathbb{K}[P,Q]$ denote the associated algebra of poset homomorphisms. **Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and projective dimension conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{reg}(\mathbb{K}[P,Q])=\mathfrak{a}(Q)\cdot (|P|-s)+s-1.
$$

$$
\operatorname{pdim}(\mathbb{K}[P,Q]) \leq \mathfrak{a}(P)\cdot (|Q|-t)+s(t-1)+1.
$$

The conjecture proposes a generalization of the previously established regularity formula for the ideals $L(P,Q)$ and predicts simultaneous formulas or bounds for their regularity and projective dimension when both posets may be disconnected. The source presents these statements as open problems; the precise definitions of $\mathfrak{a}(P)$ and $\mathfrak{a}(Q)$ should be checked in the surrounding paper.
record.source_name: Martina Juhnke-Kubitzke, Lukas Katthän and Sara Saeedi Madani, “Algebraic properties of ideals of poset homomorphisms”, arXiv:1505.07581 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.07581

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: The GLS combinatorial criterion for square-irreducibility
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{m}=\Delta_1+\dots+\Delta_k$ be a multisegment, let $C_\mathfrak{m}$ be the vector space of compatible coordinates, and let $X_\mathfrak{m}$ and $\widetilde X_\mathfrak{m}$ be the index sets defined by the multisegment. For $\lambda\in C_\mathfrak{m}$, define vectors in the vector space with basis $\{e_{i,j}:(i,j)\in\widetilde X_\mathfrak{m}\}$ by

$$
\mathsf{x}_{i,j}(\lambda):=\sum_{r:(r,j)\in X_\mathfrak{m},(i,r)\in \widetilde X_\mathfrak{m}}\lambda_{r,j}e_{i,r}-\sum_{s:(s,j)\in \widetilde X_\mathfrak{m},(i,s)\in X_\mathfrak{m}}\lambda_{i,s}e_{s,j},\qquad (i,j)\in X_\mathfrak{m}.
$$

The multisegment $\mathfrak{m}$ satisfies (GLS) when some $\lambda\in C_\mathfrak{m}$ makes these vectors linearly independent. **GLS criterion.** $Z(\mathfrak{m})$ is $\square$-irreducible if and only if $\mathfrak{m}$ satisfies (GLS). This is an equivalent reformulation of the preceding geometric conjecture and gives a criterion that the source notes is amenable to computer checking; the source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Erez Lapid and Alberto Minguez, “Geometric conditions for -irreducibility of certain representations of the general linear group over a non-archimedean local field”, arXiv:1605.08545 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.08545

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: Determinant inequality for Gaussian Markov random fields
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph. For $x
otin(-1,1)$? [sic] the paper defines $\tau(G,x)=\det(\Sigma(G,x))$, where $\Sigma(G,x)$ is the unique positive-definite matrix with diagonal entries $1$ and edge entries $x$ maximizing the determinant. **Determinant conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every $x\in[0,1)$,

$$
\tau(G,x)\geq(1-x^2)^{|E(G)|}.
$$

The inequality is verified in the paper for complete graphs and cycles, and a local version holds for $x$ in a sufficiently small interval; the general conjecture remains open.

record.title: Newman's conjecture on the maximal codensity of four-element sets
record.statement:
For a finite set $S\subseteq\mathbb Z$, let $c(S)$ be the infimum of the densities of complement sets $T$ satisfying $S+T=\mathbb Z$, and define

$$
c_k=\sup_{\{S:|S|=k\}}c(S).
$$

**Newman's conjecture.**

$$
c_4=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Newman proved the analogous values $c_3=2/5$ and $c(\{0,1,2,4\})=1/3$. Weinstein proved that $c_4<0.339934$, while a computer search confirmed the conjecture for sets of diameter at most $22$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Maria Axenovich, John Goldwasser, Bernard Lidický, Ryan R. Martin, David Offner, John Talbot and Michael Young, “Polychromatic Colorings on the Integers”, arXiv:1704.00042 (2018).

record.title: The graph positivity conjecture for random regular bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $r$-regular bipartite graph with $v=2n$ vertices, let $m_i$ denote its number of $i$-matchings, and define

$$
d(i)=\ln\left(\frac{m_i}{r^i}\right)-\ln\left(\frac{\overline{m}_i}{(v-1)^i}\right),
$$

where $\overline{m}_i$ is the number of $i$-matchings in the complete graph on the same vertices. Let $\Delta$ be the finite difference operator, so $\Delta d(i)=d(i+1)-d(i)$; graph positivity means

$$
\Delta^k d(i)\geq 0
$$

for $k=0,\ldots,v$ and $i=0,\ldots,v-k$. **Graph positivity conjecture.** As $n$ tends to infinity, the fraction of $r$-regular bipartite graphs with $2n$ vertices that satisfy graph positivity approaches one. The paper reports computer evidence for this claim, while the subsequent weak graph positivity result establishes the corresponding assertion for each fixed $i$ and $k$ rather than for all meaningful finite differences simultaneously.
record.source_name: Paul Federbush, “A Near Proof of Weak Graph Positivity, A New Property of Random Regular Graphs”, arXiv:1710.00357 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.00357

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: The characterization of graph random-walk evolution algebras
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. Let $bf{A}_{RW}(G)$ denote the evolution algebra associated with the random walk on $G$, and let $bf{A}(G)$ denote the evolution algebra associated with $G$.

**Graph evolution-algebra isomorphism conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{A}_{RW}(G)\cong \mathcal{A}(G)
$$

if and only if $G$ is regular or biregular. Moreover, if

$$
\mathcal{A}_{RW}(G)\ncong \mathcal{A}(G),
$$

then the only homomorphism between them is the null map.

The claim extends the corresponding criterion beyond the regular and biregular cases. The paper reports that it has been verified for several singular graphs, but states that further work is needed to establish it for all finite singular graphs.
record.source_name: Paula Cadavid, Mary Luz Rodiño Montoya and Pablo M. Rodríguez, “On the isomorphisms between evolution algebras of graphs and random walks”, arXiv:1710.10516 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: Palindromicity and real-rootedness conjecture for two-by-n-by-(n+1) grids
record.statement:
For every positive integer $n$, let $[r]$ denote a chain with $r$ elements and let $\mathcal{N}_{[2]\times[n]\times[n+1]}(x)$ be the antichain generating polynomial of the product poset. **Palindromicity and real-rootedness conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
\mathcal{N}_{[2]\times[n]\times[n+1]}(x)
$$

is palindromic and real-rooted, and therefore $\gamma$-positive. This is supported by computed examples and is a specialization of the broader real-rootedness phenomenon discussed in the paper; it remains open.
record.source_name: Jian Ding and Chao-Ping Dong, “Antichain generating polynomials of posets”, arXiv:1905.06692 (2019).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.06692

record.title: Conjectured Laplacian spectrum of Sierpiński graphs
record.statement:
Let $S(n,k)$ be the Sierpiński graph, with $n,k\geq 2$, and let $f$ be the polynomial defined in the source's equation for $f$. For a polynomial $g$, write $g^j$ for its $j$-fold iterate.

**Laplacian spectrum conjecture.** The Laplacian spectrum of $S(n,k)$ consists of the following eigenvalues:

1. $0$ with multiplicity $1$.
2. The zeros of $f^j(k-x)$, each with multiplicity
 
$$
\frac12\left(k^{n-j}-2k^{n-j-1}+k\right),
$$

 for $j=0,1,\ldots,n-1$.
3. The zeros of $f^j(k-x)+2$, each with multiplicity
 
$$
\frac12\left(k^{n-j-1}-1\right)(k-2),
$$

 for $j=0,1,\ldots,n-2$.

This conjecture extrapolates the explicitly computed Laplacian spectrum for the case $n=2$ from empirical evidence; the polynomial $f$ and its iterates encode the spectral values at higher levels of the Sierpiński-type graph construction.
record.source_name: Mohammad Farrokhi Derakhshandeh Ghouchan, E. Ghorbani, H. R. Maimani and F. Rahimi Mahid, “Some Algebraic Properties of Sierpiński-Type Graphs”, arXiv:1908.04037 (2020).

record.title: The power-of-two noisy Nim conjecture
record.statement: Let $N_k(p)$ denote the probability of winning from a heap of size $k$ when each transmitted binary digit is independently erroneous with probability $p$. A move transmits the number of chips left in the heap, and $k=2^n$ denotes a heap size that is a power of two. **Power-of-two noisy Nim conjecture.** If $k=2^n$, then $N_k(p)\geq \frac{1}{2}$ for all $k$. For $p\geq \frac{1}{2}$, the optimal move is to transmit $k-1$. This conjecture is based on the computed cases in the paper, and no resolution is stated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nicolas Capitelli and Melina Privitelli, “Playing through a noisy channel (and knowing it)”, arXiv:2012.06768 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.06768

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: The complete multipartite $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-distance-magic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=K_{n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_t}$ be a complete $t$-partite graph such that

$$
2^n=\sum_{i=1}^t n_i
$$

and $n_i\geq 2$ for all $i$. A $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-distance-magic labeling is a bijection from the vertices of $G$ to $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ for which all vertex weights, computed in the group, are equal. **Complete multipartite $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-distance-magic conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-distance magic. The paper proves this conjecture in the stated setting.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz and Karol Suchan, “Zero-sum partitions of Abelian groups of order 2^n”, arXiv:2111.05394 (2023).

record.title: Cycle, barbell, or theta structure conjecture for girth-achieving cycles
record.statement: Let $X$ be an arbitrary connected graph with finite girth, and let $\mathcal C$ be the set of cycle subgraphs in $\mathsf{FS}(X,\operatorname{Star}_n)$ that achieve its girth. For each $C\in\mathcal C$, let $X_C$ be the path-induced subgraph of $X$ by $C$, and set $\mathcal X=\{X_C\}_{C\in\mathcal C}$. **Cycle–barbell–theta structure conjecture.** There exists $X_C\in\mathcal X$ isomorphic to a cycle, barbell, or theta graph, and the girth is computed by the corresponding sequence of swaps around that graph. The paper states this as a desired result and supplies only partial structural discussion, leaving the assertion open.
record.source_name: Ryan Jeong, “On Structural Aspects of Friends-And-Strangers Graphs”, arXiv:2203.10337 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: Finite $N$ holographic conjecture for local operators of six-dimensional superconformal theories
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer, and let $Obs_N(0)$ denote the local operators of the theory on a stack of $N$ fivebranes wrapping $C^3$ in $R\times C^5$. Let $\mathcal G_N$ be the local $L_\infty$ algebra on $C^3$ obtained from the holographic construction, and let $\mathcal G_{N,c}$ denote its central version. The exceptional super Lie algebra $E(3|6)$ acts on these spaces. **Finite $N$ holographic conjecture.** There is an equivalence of $E(3|6)$-representations

$$
\Obs_N(0)\simeq \clie_\bu(\mathcal G_{N,c})(0).
$$

Similarly, for $N\geq 2$, let $\widetilde{\Obs}_N(0)$ denote the local operators with the center-of-mass degrees of freedom removed, and let $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_{N,c}$ be the corresponding central local $L_\infty$ algebra. Then there is an equivalence of $E(3|6)$-representations

$$
\widetilde{\Obs}_N(0)\simeq \clie_\bu(\widetilde{\mathcal G}_{N,c})(0).
$$

This conjecture identifies the local operators of the six-dimensional theory on $N$ fivebranes with the local operators computed holographically by Lie algebra cohomology. It is motivated by the expected enhancement of the holomorphically twisted superconformal algebra to the exceptional infinite-dimensional super Lie algebra $E(3|6)$ and by the holographic description of the factorization algebra of observables; the claim is presented as an expectation and no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Surya Raghavendran and Brian R. Williams, “A holographic approach to the six-dimensional superconformal index”, arXiv:2210.07910 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.07910

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

record.title: The homology conjecture for total 3-cut complexes of complete graph–cycle products
record.statement:
Let $K_m$ be the complete graph on $m$ vertices, let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\Delta_{3}^t(K_m\square C_n)$ denote their total $3$-cut complex. **The total 3-cut cycle-product homology conjecture.**

For $m\geq3$ and $n=3$,

$$
\widetilde{H}_i\bigl(\Delta_{3}^t(K_m\square C_n)\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb{Z}^{\frac{1}{2}(m^2-3m+2)},&\text{if }i=mn-6,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

For $m\geq2$ and $n\in\{4,5\}$,

$$
\widetilde{H}_i\bigl(\Delta_{3}^t(K_m\square C_n)\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb{Z}^{\frac{m-1}{2}((m-1)n^2-(m-3)n-2)},&\text{if }i=mn-6,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

For $m\geq2$ and $n\geq6$,

$$
\widetilde{H}_i\bigl(\Delta_{3}^t(K_m\square C_n)\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb{Z}^{\frac{1}{2}((m-1)^2n^2-(m^2-4m+3)n+2)},&\text{if }i=mn-6,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture is based on computed examples for total $3$-cut complexes of complete graph–cycle products; the source does not provide a resolution.
record.source_name: Pratiksha Chauhan, Samir Shukla and Kumar Vinayak, “Total 2-cut complexes of powers of cycle graphs and Cartesian products of certain graphs”, arXiv:2512.04486 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Coppersmith–Sorkin conjecture for expected k-assignment cost
record.statement:
Let $F_k(m,n)$ denote the expected cost of an optimal $k$-assignment in an $m\times n$ matrix of independent exponentially distributed random variables with mean $1$. Here a $k$-assignment is a set of $k$ entries with no two in the same row or column. **Coppersmith–Sorkin conjecture.**

$$
F_k(m,n)=\sum_{\substack{i,j\geq 0\\ i+j<k}}\frac{1}{(m-i)(n-j)}.
$$

The source says this conjecture was verified for $k\leq 6$ for arbitrary $m$ and $n$, but gives no general proof.
record.source_name: Svante Linusson and Johan Waestlund, “A Generalization of the Random Assignment Problem”, arXiv:math/0006146 (2000).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2000). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0004175](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0004175).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0006146

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2000).

record.title: Complementary-response conjecture for subset take-away
record.statement: Let $A$ be a finite set, and consider the subset take-away game in which players alternately choose proper, non-empty subsets of $A$, with no chosen set containing a set chosen earlier; a player unable to move loses. For an opening move $S\subsetneq A$, let $A\setminus S$ be its complementary move. **Complementary-response conjecture.** A winning response to an opening move is to play the complementary move. The paper reports computer verification of this response for the relevant case when $|A|=6$, after Gale's conjecture had been verified for smaller starting positions, but gives no resolution of the general conjecture.
record.source_name: J. Daniel Christensen and Mark Tilford, “David Gale's subset take-away game”, arXiv:math/0207185 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207185

record.title: The twisted and column-even domino-plane-partition bijection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\GCSPP{n,m}$ be the set of twisted domino plane partitions and let $\CDPP{n,m}$ be the set of restricted domino plane partitions with all columns of even length. Let $\overline U_1$ denote the statistic counting the relevant $1$-parts.

**Twisted domino correspondence conjecture.** For non-negative integers $m$ and $n\geq1$, there should be a bijection

$$
\GCSPP{n,m}\longleftrightarrow\CDPP{n,m}
$$

that preserves $\overline U_1$; in particular, the two sets should have the same cardinality and the statistic should have the same distribution.

The conjecture is supported by agreement of computed cardinalities for $n\leq6$. The source does not provide a proof or a general construction of the bijection.
record.source_name: Masao Ishikawa, “On refined enumerations of totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions II”, arXiv:math/0606082 (2006).

record.title: The QQR code duality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p>5$ be an odd prime, let $Q,N\subset GF(p)^\times$ be the quadratic residues and non-residues, and let $C_{NQ}$ be the quasi-quadratic residue code

$$
C_{NQ}=\{(r_Nr_S,r_Qr_S):S\subseteq GF(p)\}\subset {\mathbb F}^{2p},
$$

where ${\mathbb F}=GF(2)$. **The QQR code duality conjecture.** If $p\equiv1\pmod4$, then $C_{NQ}\oplus C_{NQ}^{\perp}={\mathbb F}^{2p}$ and $C_{NQ}\cap C_{NQ}^{\perp}=\{\mathbf 0\}$; if $p\equiv3\pmod4$, then $C_{NQ}^{\perp}=C_{NQ}$. The claim is based on computer computations and concerns whether these quasi-quadratic residue codes are complementary or self-dual according to the congruence class of $p$; no proof is supplied.
record.source_name: David Joyner, “On quadratic residue codes and hyperelliptic curves”, arXiv:math/0609562 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609562

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

record.title: The formally self-dual extension conjecture for QQR codes
record.statement: Let $p>5$ be an odd prime, let $C_{NQ}\subset {\mathbb F}^{2p}$ be the quasi-quadratic residue code, and let $C'$ be the code spanned by $C_{NQ}$ and the all-ones codeword. Let $A=[A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n]$ be the weight distribution vector of $C_{NQ}$, and define $A^*=[A_n,A_{n-1},\ldots,A_0]$. **The formally self-dual extension conjecture.** If $p\equiv1\pmod4$, then $C'$ is formally self-dual, has dimension $p$, and its weight distribution vector is $A+A^*$. The claim is presented as supported by computer computations, with no proof supplied.
record.source_name: David Joyner, “On quadratic residue codes and hyperelliptic curves”, arXiv:math/0609562 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609562

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).
